steps.content: You're led into a duty room nearby. Soon, egg pancakes, minced meat, and hot bean soup appear before you. There seems to be coffee heating up on the stove as well.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: When was the last time you ate?
...Last night, I had some grilled chicken, bean curd, and a piece of meat from Tally.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: And the last time you slept?
...Yesterday afternoon, in the wooden box in Romanesque.
You didn't say that out loud, but she doesn't seem like she needs to hear it either. She just sighs.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Here are some quick snacks, I know you're in a hurry. I don't think I can get you to lie down either. Try to take a nap on the railcar, and make up for the rest with coffee.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: This is what Julien drinks when he pulls several all-nighters in a row. He puts ten sugar cubes in a cup to replenish his brain energy.
Under her gaze, you begin chewing silently. In fact, you can't really taste anything, but you swallow mechanically. Like she said, your body is reaching its limit.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: People have some misunderstanding about you. News about the battle at noon has probably started spreading. Taran shouted so loudly that those words must have gotten out. Those who've heard it may think you're an infiltrated spy.

steps.speaker: Taran
steps.content: Stop! This is the expert you're looking for, the chief of Minos Bureau of Crisis Control, the hero that helped you take down the Legion.

steps.speaker: Donald
steps.content: You think it's fair to trade me for their trust?! We came for the same mission, taking care of Drifter Camp, didn't we?

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Don't be fooled by the brutal way they fight. Most of the people in the camp are ordinary folks who get scared easily. They didn't even dare to face gangsters in the past, let alone that huge thing today.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: They have nothing against you. It's just that they've been through too much. Fear has become a habit.
She smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Blame it on Julien, that sulky guy. He only knows to hide behind those mechanisms whenever something happens. He should at least say a few big words to lift the morale, being the leader and all.
The way his subordinate mocks him prompts you to rethink your preconception of Rustfire's leader.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Then again, if even Julien, the most paranoid person in the camp, is willing to team with you, the others will gradually understand and accept you too. Don't worry.
She knows how to gain the trust from others. Hella probably can't resist her moves either. But you're not in the mood to hear all this. You only want to leave as soon as possible.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We're only cooperating and getting what we need from each other. You don't need to comfort me.
When you finish, you pick up the bowl of bean soup and down it. Behind the bowl, after a brief silence, she suddenly laughs.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Didn't expect you to be a stubborn kid too.
<size=44>?</size>

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Deep down, you're feeling aggrieved, but you just swallow that feeling and continues to do your job. Has this happened to you often?
Before you retort, her eyes dim.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: My kid was about your age when she left.
You swallow the words before they escape your mouth. Even if it's just acting, the sadness in her eyes is too infectious. You can't bring yourself to say it.

steps.speaker: Options
options: ...Was it the Executive Committee? Or the sheriffs?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's why you joined Rustfire...?

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Don't overthink. It has nothing to do with people on your side. It was many years ago. I've long gotten over it.
She pauses and stands up to get the coffee. She also grabs some sugar cubes for you and sets them on the side.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: I joined Rustfire to be the mother of more kids. Like you, they all don't know how to take care of themselves. My work is never done.

steps.speaker: Options
options: ...Thank you for taking care of me.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: ...No. You're neither my child nor our companion.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Thank you.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: They had an urgent assembly today, saying they had to fight against a monster. I heard explosions and gunshots. The depot was in ruins and fire was blazing... Julien told me to prepare for the worst, I thought...
Her hands holding the coffee cup begin trembling.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: No matter your identity, stance, and purpose... You showed up and protected us.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: No outsiders have ever stayed for us, and even now, you're still straining yourself to keep working.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: I didn't lose anyone else, and it's all thanks to you. Regardless of what the others say, I'm... <size=40>truly grateful</size> to you.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: The second sentence of the post-episode, no background
The first sentence of the post-episode, no background
...It finally tastes like something.

steps.speaker: (Scene change)
steps.content: (Scene change)
When you walk out of the duty room, the logistics officer shoves several more wraps at you and returns to her usual kind and somewhat strict self.
Hella is staring in a certain direction with Hecate, wielding her pipe and cursing.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: It's that jerk that abducted us! He was following us. Who knows what he's up to this time.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Oh, Taran? He got scolded by Julien. He's probably holding his temper and has come here to be your bodyguard. That kid's quite skillful in operating mechanisms. He could be useful.

steps.speaker: Hecate
steps.content: I don't trust him. He's hostile toward Chief.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: He's just stubborn. Don't mind him, and don't waste your energy on him. Once his seniors from the elite squad are back, someone will deal with him.
You look at Taran. He can't hear your shouts from where he stands, so Hella's cursing doesn't do much. But he should be able to see your hands clearly, perhaps you can sign something at him...

steps.speaker: Options
options: Wag your index finger to mock him
Be a reasonable adult and leave him alone

steps.content: You're not sure if he sees your sign. Anyway, he turns to leave once you're done.
You'll teach him a lesson when your work is done.

steps.speaker: Hella & Hecate
steps.content:
Pff.
Hmm?

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Hahaha. Let's go.
You can't see Taran's reaction clearly, but from the way the pink-haired fighter next to him holds down his shoulders... the kid's likely mad.
You leave contentedly. You have business to tend to. You'll come back to this later.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: Where do you want to go for your investigation next? Want me to show you those executive officers' messages?
Your body is warming up again. Your stuffed chest is slowly relaxing. The stuck cogs in your brain begin turning gradually. You start thinking again and clues are finally popping up in your head.

steps.speaker: Options
options: No need. It has nothing to do with them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Both the grievance-loaded executive officers and the shocking, terrifying contamination are all just tricks used by the mastermind behind to aggravate you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: They're not done yet. Once they use up all the executive officers, they'll switch to another type of performance.
As you speak, you hear a clamor mixed with moans and cries for help from a distance. Lavina's communications device sounds.

steps.speaker: Lavina
steps.content: What? Corruptor outbreaks in multiple locations? This...
Before she can react, a gust of moldy-smelling wind sweeps over the garden you're in. A pitch-black flame ignites fear instantly.
